title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
description:
Two lists of integers are each already sorted in non-decreasing order. Combine them into a single list that is also sorted in non-decreasing order, and print it.

Input format
Line 1: n and m, the lengths of the two lists.
Line 2: the n integers of the first list.
Line 3: the m integers of the second list.

Output format
The n + m integers of the merged list, separated by single spaces.
constraints: 1 <= n, m <= 100000. Values are between -1000000000 and 1000000000. Duplicates are allowed.
hints: Both lists are already sorted, so you should not need to sort the whole combined list again.
Compare the front elements of the two lists, output the smaller one, and move forward in that list only.
Keep two indices i and j. While both lists have items left, append the smaller of a[i] and b[j] and advance that index. When one list runs out, append the rest of the other.

examples.explanation: Taking the smaller front value each time gives 1, 2, 3, 4, 9, 10.
Equal values from both lists all appear in the output.
